title: Community flow packages - third-party Flows as data-only folders dropped into user_flows/
description:
TARGETS 1.6. Let the community author Flows the way plugin developers extend ZBrush and Blender: third-party devs push the app for free because they want to sell their own work. Cubric Vision never sells anything and stays free; Mad Pony Interactive may sell its own Flows as any third party would.

A package is a folder dropped into user_flows/ - restart and it appears. Manifest JSON + workflow JSON + optional images. No Python, no pip, no custom node repos. Devs use only nodes and models Cubric already ships; anything missing is a request MPI may accept or decline (route those through public GitHub issues with public decisions - the platform owner picking what ships is visible, and transparency defuses it).

KEY INSIGHT: the op a Flow registers across 4 files (commandRegistry.js, universal_workflows.js, operationRegistry.js, operation_registry.json) is PURE DATA - mediaInputs is an array of {key, mediaType, title, required}. So a user Flow's op is built from its manifest at load time and no registry file is ever edited. Ids from user_flows/ are namespaced on load (user:<id>) against collision.

SCOPE: user_flows/ loader; manifest schema (FlowDef + op fields + compat block + author/homepage/licence); load-time validator; developer docs (injection rules, the Input_*/Output_* title law); generated node lockfile; port the remaining uiComponent Flow and retire the field. MPI republishes one of its own Flows as a package to prove the path.

VALIDATOR is developer experience, not security. A scan of all 14 bundled node packs found no URL/HTTP/download node classes (only ComfyUI's own SaveImageWebsocket, which writes to the connected app), so a workflow JSON has no phone-home vector today - re-run that scan whenever a pack is adopted. It exists because the injector SILENTLY SKIPS an Input_* title with no matching node, so a broken flow otherwise fails as a mystery. Checks: node class in the bundled set; Input_*/Output_* title law (reuse validate-injection-rules.mjs); declared requiredModels/requiredDeps ids exist; no absolute paths baked into widget values. Ship the same script to devs as a pre-publish linter.

DEV NODE PACK: do not fork or vendor the 14 packs (staleness + redistribution). js/data/modelConstants/nodesDeps.js already pins every pack by repo + tag/commit - GENERATE a lockfile + installer from it so a dev's ComfyUI matches the shipped engine exactly. Same list feeds the validator allowlist.

DEPRECATION UX: an installed Flow ALWAYS shows, disabled, with the reason named ("Needs nvidia-pid, removed in 1.5"). Silence reads as a broken app. Keeping a third-party Flow working is the dev's job - no shims, no migrations; a user who needs an abandoned Flow pins an older portable build, exactly as Blender users do. Needs the tombstone ledger card.

1.7+ (NOT this card): an optional GitHub registry repo where devs register a Flow; entries baked into the next release as Community Flows cards linking out to the dev's own page. Advertising only - never a payment rail, no accounts, no checkout, no VAT/MOSS, no merchant status. Flows work unregistered, so it is off the critical path.

VOCABULARY: "plugin" already means capability model here (image-describer shipped; MPI-507 converts PiD into four upscale plugins; plugin-dep GC tests exist). Third-party packages are FLOWS. Never "flow plugins".

LICENCE: AGPL-3.0 and ComfyUI's GPL-3.0 both permit selling; paid GPL Blender addons are the precedent. A package is data - mere aggregation, not a derivative of the app - so bundling does not force AGPL onto it. No DRM is possible; buyers may legally redistribute. MPI Flows shipped free stay free; monetisation, if ever, is a separate paid package with its own id, additive only. Preserve that option by authoring MPI's sellable Flows in their OWN repo under their own licence, not inside the AGPL app repo.

RELATED: the 1.5 package-ready-flows card (its prerequisite), MPI-529, MPI-306, MPI-304 (requiredDeps), MPI-528 (licensing surface).
